4. The plaint case is that one Asiruddin was the owner of the suit land appertaining to RS khatian No. 271 Mouja Fetemagos Talluk Ghagra, Panchagar (previously District Panchagar). The said Asiruddin died leaving behind 3 sons Tumijuddin and others, wife Asma Khatun and daughter Jahura Khatun as his legal heirs. Tumijuddin sold 1.66 acres of land to the plaintiff No.1 on 6-3-1982. Tumijuddin and his mother Asma Khatun sold 0.41 acres to Alauddin, Sahadut and Moshiar Rahman. The said Alauddin, Sahadut and Moshiar Rahman died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 2-28 as their legal heirs. The said Tumijuddin and his mother Jahura Khatun sold 0.17 acres of land to one Eiad Ali died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 40-42 as to the legal heirs. The aforementioned plaintiffs are possessing the land ejmali. One Rafiqueuddin as the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1-6 filed the Title Suit No.48 of 82 as vendor of the abovementioned land and the said suit was decreed exparte on 16-9-1982, which was not known to plaintiffs as they were not party when the above plaintiffs went for mutation they came to know about the abovementioned exparte decree. 

 5. The said suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-10 by filing the written statement denying the statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that one Hedaiatullah was the originally owner of the suit land along with other land measuring 68.64 acres. One Naziruddin bought the said land on auction and the said land was given pattan on the 2ild Asar, 1348 BS by to Ojiuddin Prodhan for the land measuring 4.44 acres and the land was recorded in his name. During the period of S.A. khatian the land was wrongly recorded in the name of one Asruddin Prodhan also known as Asamuddin instead of Ojiuddin Prodhan. The said Ojiuddin Prodhan died leaving behind his son Rafiquuddin as his heirs. The said Asam Uddin tried to dispossess. The defendant came to know that SA recorded of right was published in the name of Asiruddin, therefore, the Title Suit No. 48 of 1982 was filed against the heirs of Asam Uddin in the Court of the then Munsif, Panchagar wherein Tumijuddin, Jajura Khatun and Asma Khatun were made defendants. The mother and the sister of Rafiquddin were also made the defendants. After service of the notices upon the defendants they appeared in the suit by filing a written statement and also sought adjournment on 15-9-1982 but the learned Judge by rejecting the said application passed the ex parte decree on 16-9-1982. 

 13. I have examined the factual aspects both of the parties and I have found that the present petitioner claimed that they are the successors of the auction purchaser of the suit land, but I found that the present defendant-petitioner failed to produce any document as to this auction purchase and the subsequent transfer of the suit land in their favour. Whereas, the plaintiff-opposite-parties adduced as many as 3 PWs and also filed the documents in support of their cases being exhibit 1 series to exhibit 5 series and from those exhibit it appears that the predecessors of the present opposite-parties had the record of right in the S.A. khatian, which is exhibited marked as 3(1). Moreover, the present plaintiff-opposite-parties produced document as to the record of right being rent receipt exhibits 4 & 4(1). The present plaintiff opposite-parties claimed their title through 3 deeds dated 19-12-1981 exhibit 1 7-1-1982 exhibit 2 and 6-3-1982 exhibit 1(kha) for their ownership upon the suit land.
